sections.heading: Added
items: Each running copy of the app gets its own webview data directory, so two windows opened at once no longer fight over one profile — on Windows the engine takes an exclusive lock on it, and the second instance would fail to start. Directories from past runs are pruned on launch, using a lock file each instance holds open rather than the directory's timestamp: a session left open overnight looks untouched from the outside.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Signing in no longer leaves a zombie `az login` process behind on every attempt. The child is reaped, and its exit is also what tells the app the browser flow finished — or was abandoned.
A corrupt cache file costs a cold start and nothing else, instead of a nonsensical "scanned N ago".

sections.heading: Changed
items: CI pipeline only — no user-visible change.

sections.heading: Added
items: Windows support: an installer, and CI that builds and publishes it with every release.

sections.heading: Changed
items: The update check identifies itself with a versioned User-Agent and marks the request as coming from the updater, which is what separates a new install from an existing user updating in the download logs.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Long lane names are truncated with a tooltip carrying the full name, instead of overflowing the trace view.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: A correlation id is bound to the field it was found in. Matching the same value in an unrelated column used to pull steps into a trace that were never part of it.

sections.heading: Added
items: The update check resolves the artifact for the platform it is running on, so the banner offers the macOS, Windows or Linux build directly instead of the download page.

sections.heading: Changed
items: Internal: Azure sign-in consolidated into one `start_login` path, so the welcome screen and the session check no longer implement it twice.

sections.heading: Changed
items: The Windows installer runs with the lowest privileges by default, so it installs per-user without a UAC prompt. Machine-wide installation stays available through a command-line option.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: The app adopts the login shell's `PATH`, so `az` is found when it is launched from Finder or the Start menu rather than from a terminal.

sections.heading: Added
items: Subscriptions that cannot be read, and sessions that have expired, are reported as what they are instead of showing as an empty workspace list.
